source.title: Improving Sparse-View 3DGS Generalization via Flat Minima Optimization
source.authors: Kangmin Seo; Sangeek Hyun; MinKyu Lee; Jae-Pil Heo

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates flat-minima-style perturbation and its relation to train-view and test-view rendering robustness in 3D Gaussian Splatting, extending the idea to a different representation and task.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own rendering and perturbation-robustness results. Cited findings about neural-network flat minima and other prior methods are not recorded as results. No claim version directly covers 3DGS rendering; its findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses flat-minima principles to develop a 3D Gaussian Splatting training method and evaluates rendering quality and positional-perturbation robustness. It does not test any specified version. In particular, V7 concerns magnitude-aware weight sharpness ranking classification generalization gaps among convolutional networks; Gaussian-position robustness and rendering PSNR do not measure that claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: scale-adaptive stochastic positional perturbations, magnitude scheduling, and periodic reinitialization improve sparse-view 3DGS rendering quality, stability, and novel-view generalization. This is a conclusion about their training framework, not validation of V7's sharpness-ranking claim.
record.recipe_differences: Applies scale-adaptive positional perturbation and periodic reinitialization to 3D Gaussian Splatting; the paper's task and model representation differ from the neural-network claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and input-view setting; perturbation magnitude; perturbation distribution and parameter; stochastic versus mixed-loss strategy; magnitude scheduling; periodic reinitialization; results vary with view count and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: On LLFF with three input views, the proposed method reportedly suffers smaller training- and test-view PSNR drops under post-training Gaussian-position perturbations than 3DGS and DropGaussian. DropGaussian's test-view degradation nearly matches 3DGS. Exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with scale-adaptive stochastic positional perturbations and periodic reinitialization can improve robustness to subsequent positional perturbations.

record.problems: The perturbation-robustness values are presented in a figure without numerical values in the text. The evidence is for 3DGS rendering, not the neural-network settings in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted: other reported tables compare reconstruction metrics or ablate the proposed 3DGS method, but do not measure a claim version's named behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level generalization under random labels.
Width increases beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout effects on classifier test error, including training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation conditions.

Magnitude-aware weight perturbations ranking training–test classification error gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and measuring test-accuracy changes.

record.verdict_notes: No claim-version results are missing. Other reconstruction comparisons and ablations are declared in rows_left_out and fall outside all versions. The broader improvement narrative has exceptions: Mip-NeRF360 with 36 views is worse than vanilla 3DGS on all three reported metrics, and some other comparisons improve PSNR or SSIM while worsening LPIPS.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the listed neural network architectures.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

The specified comparison among convolutional networks using magnitude-aware weight perturbations and training/test error gaps; this study instead perturbs Gaussian positions in 3DGS and reports rendering degradation under perturbation.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
